newsitem.title: PERU: Peru prepares new, reduced GDP measure for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Peru prepares new, reduced GDP measure for 1997.

text.p: The Peruvian government is preparing a new measurement of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) that will reduce the current over-valued total of $60 billion to between $40 billion and $45 billion, officials said Thursday.
They added that the new measure, to be used from the beginning of 1997, would use 1994 as the base year for the indices used in the GDP calculation.
The current measure uses a base year of 1979, which analysts and government officials agree has caused a distortion in the gross figure.
The government's National Institute of Statistics and Information (INEI) is responsible for compiling the GDP figures in conjunction with the economy ministry and the central reserve bank.
Under the current GDP calculations, nine-month growth was 1.9 percent and is expected to end the year below three percent, compared to 7.0 percent in 1995 and 13.1 percent in 1994.
